summary: Full first-pass regression on Sophie+Ken RSVP + Rehearsal Dinner rebuild. 24/24 pytest backend tests pass and every prioritised UI flow verified via Playwright: lookup normalization (whitespace/case/apostrophe/curly-apostrophe/hyphen/collapsed), not-found editorial copy, ambiguous disambiguation by email and by member name, returning-guest 'Welcome back.' interstitial, party confirm, per-person attendance, submit + update-in-place, plus-one gating, cross-party guest_id injection rejection, uninvited event_response rejection, admin auth 401, admin overview with separate Rehearsal Dinner block, admin parties search + filter, CSV export, deadline enforcement (past deadline closes RSVP + rejects submit; deadline restored to null after test). RSVP wizard: Sophie Knochenhauer shows step '02 / 06' with overline 'The night before', title 'Rehearsal Dinner', and 'Details to follow.' (no invented details). Aunt Gail shows '02 / 05' with zero mention of 'rehearsal' anywhere on the page.

minor.issue: meal_totals is populated from guests.meal_choice regardless of settings.meal_options_enabled. If a guest still holds a stale meal_choice from a previous settings state (currently 'Seared salmon (sample) × 1' visible), it leaks into the dashboard while meal options are disabled. Consider gating the meal_totals aggregation on meal_options_enabled OR clearing guest.meal_choice when it is no longer in the allowlist.

action_items: (minor) Gate meal_totals aggregation on meal_options_enabled OR clear guest.meal_choice when settings change so disabled meal state doesn't display stale counts in the admin overview.

(informational) Preview DB now contains extra responses from testing agents (Jamie Doe-Smith declined, Sophie Knochenhauer attending RD, Test Guest party from earlier smoke tests, Alex Sample lookup unchanged). No action required — returning-guest path handles this.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1500 lines; consider splitting into routers/ (guest_lookup, rsvp, admin, admin_import, models, security). Not blocking.

Line 636-637: right after upsert with $setOnInsert submitted_at, code re-checks and calls a second $set — this is a no-op if the party existed (submitted_at already set) but harmless. $setOnInsert on a non-upsert $set was silently ignored anyway; the follow-up $set is what actually persists submitted_at on first submission. Clean but slightly confusing; a single conditional set would read better.
guest_lookup disambiguation-by-member searches only against the candidate parties' non-plus-one members using the same three lookup keys — correct and safe.
member_events correctly omits the 'events' key entirely for non-invited members (verified in tests) — good defense against enumeration.
admin_export CSV column 'Rehearsal Dinner' emits 'Invited' when RD-invited but no response yet — nice touch.
